summary: The work-action fence now judges the claim's own incarnation instead of the seat's newest runtime record. A record another host made of its own old runtime, for a seat that has since moved, no longer refuses the live incarnation's work actions or stops its driver's lease renewals. The seat's selected actual source also never picks such an end over the desired host's record

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged: latest_actual_at and current_harness_at keep their folds (#4769 records that part).

compatibility.detail: Fence direction: it accepts more than before, never less where today's rule accepted. A work action (claim, renew, progress, wait, resume, extend, complete, fail, release) from an incarnation whose own runtime records show it running and whose own harness has not ended is accepted even when a newer runtime record from another host describes another, ended incarnation. These are still refused: an incarnation replaced by a newer running one, its own end from any host, an end naming no incarnation from the host where it runs, an incarnation never observed running (including one whose records say only `starting`, which the old fence refused too), another actor, and a lease another incarnation holds. Drivers renew the claims their own incarnation holds while their provider runs, without reading the seat's current harness first.

recovery.detail: An older daemon judges the seat's newest runtime record, as before; an older driver asks for the seat's current harness before renewing, as before.
